title: Brother Scan Button Not Working
cardText: Troubleshoot a Brother printer or scanner that will not scan to a Windows computer when the Scan button is pressed.
Check computer scanning, Brother ControlCenter, scan-event settings and device communication.
Resolve problems that may require reinstalling the complete Brother software package.
text: This guide is for Brother printers and scanners where scanning from the device control panel does not work correctly.
The steps focus on scanning to a Windows computer using Brother software.
ControlCenter availability and menu names vary by model. Some newer models use Brother iPrint&Scan instead.
First establish whether scanning works from the computer before troubleshooting the Scan button.

testComputerScanning.title: Test scanning from the computer
body: Open Brother ControlCenter, Brother iPrint&Scan, or another compatible scanning application on the computer.
Try scanning a document directly from the computer.
This determines whether the scanner itself is communicating with Windows.
testComputerScanning.alt: Brother iPrint&Scan software showing the Scan button
testComputerScanning.caption: Brother iPrint&Scan. The scanning interface may differ depending on the software version.

checkScannerConnection.title: Check the scanner connection
body: Confirm the Brother printer or scanner is powered on and showing no errors.
For USB connections, check the cable and try another USB port.
For network connections, confirm the printer and computer are connected to the correct network.
Check whether Windows detects the scanner.

resolveConnection.title: Resolve scanner communication problem
body: The computer cannot reliably communicate with the scanner.
Check the USB cable, network connection, printer IP address and Windows device detection as appropriate.
Restore communication before troubleshooting the Scan button.
Once the connection is working, restart this guide.

checkScannerDriver.title: Check the scanner driver
body: Confirm the scanner driver for the Brother model is installed.
Check whether the scanner is available in Brother software or Windows scanning applications.
If the printer can print but cannot scan, the scanner driver or scanning components may be missing.

link.name: Brother support and downloads
link.description: Find the correct scanner driver and software for your Brother model.

checkBrotherSoftware.title: Check Brother scanning software
body: Confirm Brother ControlCenter or the model's supported Brother scanning application is installed.
Open the application manually and check whether the scanner is detected.
Some Brother models use ControlCenter4, while others use Brother iPrint&Scan.
The printer Scan button may require additional Brother components beyond a basic Windows scanner driver.

link.name: Brother software and driver downloads
link.description: Find the software available for your exact printer model.

checkBrotherSoftware.caption: Example Brother ControlCenter4 interface.

installBrotherSoftware.title: Install the Brother scanning software
body: Download the appropriate software package for the exact Brother model from Brother's official support website.
Where available, use the complete driver and software package rather than only a basic printer driver.
Install the required scanning components and follow the connection instructions.
After installation, test scanning from the computer.

link.name: Brother support downloads
link.description: Select your printer model and download the compatible driver and scanning software.

checkScanDestination.title: Check the Scan button destination
body: On the Brother printer, open the Scan menu.
Select the appropriate option, such as Scan to PC or Scan to File.
If a computer list appears, confirm the correct Windows computer is available and selected.
Check whether the computer name has changed or the printer is trying to send the scan to an old computer.
checkScanDestination.alt: Brother printer control panel showing the Scan option
checkScanDestination.caption: Example Brother printer touchscreen showing the Scan option. The destination selection may vary by model.

checkDeviceRegistration.title: Check computer registration and network discovery
body: Confirm Brother scanning software recognises the correct printer or scanner.
For network-connected scanners, check that the PC and printer can communicate over the network.
Check any Brother setting for registering the computer as a Scan to PC destination, where supported.
If the PC is not listed, restart Brother scanning software and check the device selection settings.

link.name: Brother troubleshooting and support
link.description: Find model-specific instructions for Scan to PC and network scanning problems.

checkScanEvents.title: Check scan-event settings
body: Open Brother ControlCenter4 and locate the Device Settings tab, then Device Scan Settings, where available.
Confirm the required Scan to File, Scan to Image or other destination is configured.
Where supported, check the settings for starting scanning from the printer's control panel.
Check that the Brother background scanning software is running.
Apply any changes before testing the printer Scan button again.

link.name: Configure ControlCenter4 and the Scan button
link.description: Official Brother instructions showing how to change the settings used by the printer's Scan button.

checkScanEvents.alt: Brother ControlCenter4 Device Scan Settings window
checkScanEvents.caption: Example Device Scan Settings window for configuring the printer's Scan button.

configureScanEvents.title: Configure scan events
body: Select the appropriate Scan button destination in the Brother software.
Configure the destination folder, application or file format as required.
Enable any relevant control-panel scanning option supported by the model.
Save the settings and return to the printer.

link.name: Brother Scan button settings instructions
link.description: Step-by-step instructions for configuring ControlCenter4 Device Scan Settings.

testScanButton.title: Test scanning from the printer
body: Place a document on the scanner glass or in the automatic document feeder.
Press Scan on the Brother printer.
Choose the configured scanning destination and select the correct computer if prompted.
Check whether the scanning process starts and the document reaches the computer.

scanButtonFixed.title: Scan button working
body: The Brother Scan button successfully sends scans to the computer.
The scanner connection, software and scan destination are functioning correctly.

reinstallBrotherPackage.title: Reinstall the complete Brother software package
body: The Scan button still fails after checking Brother software and scan-event settings.
Download the complete Brother driver and software package for the exact printer model and Windows version.
Run the installer over the existing installation where the installer supports this.
This may repair missing or damaged Brother components and Scan button integration without requiring a manual uninstall first.
Restart the computer if requested, then test scanning from the printer again.

link.name: Brother full driver and software downloads
link.description: Select your Brother printer model to find the complete software package supported for your version of Windows.

reinstallBrotherPackage.alt: Brother support download page showing the Full Driver and Software Package
reinstallBrotherPackage.caption: Look for the Full Driver & Software Package when it is available for your model.

finalDiagnosis.title: Further Brother scanner diagnostics required
body: The problem remains after checking scanner communication, Brother software and Scan button configuration.
Record the exact Brother printer model, Windows version, connection type and any displayed error.
Check Brother's model-specific troubleshooting documentation or contact Brother support.
Further diagnosis may involve model-specific network settings, Windows security software, scanner drivers or damaged Brother components.

link.name: Brother New Zealand Support
link.description: Find troubleshooting articles, downloads and contact options for your printer.
